subject: Cold-start spikes on Hosted GPU autoscale causing p95/p99 regressions — BrightLeaf escalation
messages:
From: BrightLeaf Support <support@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: laura@brightleafhealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes — production impact

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing intermittent large latency spikes (p95 and p99) on the Hosted API for our production workspace around 08:50 PST this morning. Impact: timeouts for synchronous features and a 3x error-rate increase for short-text routes.

From our side it looks tied to autoscaling events — when additional GPUs spin up we see a ~15-25s window where many requests jump to p99. Attaching a sample trace and a latency histogram.

Observed:
- p50 ~80ms unchanged
- p95 moved from 420ms to 2.2s during spikes
- p99 moved from 1.1s to 7.5s during spikes
- Error rate (5xx) increased from 0.4% to 3.6% in the spike windows

We are in production and this is customer-facing. Can you confirm root cause and an ETA for a mitigation?

Thanks,
Laura Park
Product Manager, BrightLeaf Health

[Attachment: latency_hist.png]

Subject: Fwd: Intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes — production impact (BrightLeaf)

Forwarding BrightLeaf's report — they correlate spikes with autoscale events. Monica/Markus/Grace: can you triage?

Priority: P0 for us — customer on PLG -> enterprise conversion. If we can't stabilize quickly we risk churn.

Initial asks:
- Quick diagnosis: are these cold-starts (kernel compile, model init, KV cache warm)?
- Short-term mitigation: can we alter autoscaling policy or pre-warm GPU instances?
- Exec flag: if we need to temporarily provision reserved capacity, I'll escalate.

Rishi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes — BrightLeaf

Thanks Rishi — looking at the attached traces and our dashboards. Early notes:

- The spike aligns with autoscaler activity: new GPU nodes are entering the pool at 08:49–08:51.
- Warm-up items: model weights load (~4–6s), JIT/kernel linking (6–9s on first request shapes), and KV-cache population for prefix-heavy requests (~4–8s). These overlap and can sum to the 15–25s window that BrightLeaf sees.
- We see a higher incidence on short prompts where batching is lower and the runtime can't amortize kernel overhead.

Short-term mitigations I can action now:
1) Increase min warm instances in the target pool for BrightLeaf's requests (raise from 0 to 1–2) — quick config change, low risk.
2) Enable aggressive pre-warm: fire synthetic requests to newly created nodes to trigger kernel/link paths and KV warming.
3) Route critical short-prompt traffic to a pinned warm variant (smaller model quantized) while we stabilize.

I recommend 1 + 2 immediately; I'll coordinate with Markus to enable a pre-warm hook and run a smoke test.

[No attachments in this message]

—Monica
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes — BrightLeaf

I've pulled the autoscaler and runtime logs for the BrightLeaf pool. Key data attached.

Findings:
- Autoscaler spin-up latency median: 12s, 95th: 21s (node readiness + CUDA context init).
- First-inference latency spike coincides with kernel JIT + empty KV-cache warm path.
- There's a throttling loop in our orchestration where up to 2 additional seconds are spent waiting for health checks on particular driver versions.

Attachment: autoscale_timeline.csv (per-node timestamps, init steps)

I can implement the pre-warm hook in the next 20 minutes and update the warm-min to 1 for the pool. Will monitor p95/p99 and report back.

Markus
Runtime Team Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Escalation: BrightLeaf — exec approval for temporary reserved capacity

Looping Evelyn — BrightLeaf is at risk of degradation during peak hours. Monica and Markus have a remediation plan (pre-warm and min-warm node config) but we may need an interim capacity reservation to avoid autoscaler churn overnight while we validate.

Risks: churn/loss for a large potential account mid-PG. Recommended temporary action: allocate 2 reserved GPUs for the BrightLeaf workspace for 48–72 hours while we run validation and a full patch to reduce cold-start time.

Estimated incremental cost: ~$1.2k/day (onboarding reserved instances, region us-west). If approved, we will bill as a temporary credit and review with finance.

Grace

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Action plan: Immediate mitigations + 72h reserved capacity (BrightLeaf)

Laura — quick update and plan: thank you for the traces. We reproduced the spike pattern tied to autoscaler warmups. Immediate steps we are taking (timeline in hours):

1) Now — raise min warm instances for your pool to 1 and enable pre-warm hook to exercise kernel/JIT paths (Monica/Markus). Expected impact: majority of the p95/p99 spikes eliminated within 30–60 minutes.
2) Hour 1–3 — monitor traffic, run synthetic short-prompt tests and review p95/p99. We'll share live Grafana link.
3) Hour 0–72 — temporary reserved capacity: we have approval for up to 72 hours to keep 2 GPUs hot and avoid autoscaler churn while we implement a longer-term fix.
4) 72h+ — postmortem and permanent changes: runtime JIT caching, driver health-check optimization, and model variant routing for short prompts. Owner: Monica (postmortem), Markus (runtime fixes).

I've attached a short mutual action plan and a draft SLA adjustment for the temporary window. We'll apply a goodwill credit for any customer-impact minutes today while we restore stable p99 behavior.

Attachments: MAP_BrightLeaf_20261115.docx, SLA_adjustment_draft.pdf

Expected next update within 60 minutes.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Action plan: Immediate mitigations + 72h reserved capacity (BrightLeaf) — update

Update after rolling pre-warm + min-warm change:

- We enabled pre-warm hooks at 10:05 PST and set pool min-warm to 1.
- Observed p95 returned to baseline within two autoscaler events; p99 improved from 7.5s to ~1.2s.
- Error-rate spike resolved; 5xx dropped back to ~0.6%.
- Kept 2 reserved GPUs active as approved; will taper after 48 hours if stable.

Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosting/brightleaf-prod-latency (live)
JIRA: INF-7245 - follow-up runtime optimization (owners: Markus, Monica)

Closing this escalation for now; initiating a postmortem and permanent runtime patch workstream.

Markus
Runtime Team Lead, Redwood Inference
